summary:
Status: the csharp review is finished. Every step of review.md ran on a copy (P/reviews/csharp/ws). The porter's tree was left untouched, and the copy ends clean with pages byte-identical to the porter's.

The port is honest and its numbers reproduce exactly. Build 0 with a clean tree, guard 4/4, guard plus reader 81/81, suite 2630/2635 with 0 failures, golden 2/2, reviewed one command exit 1 with only rootquick defect 3, SCRATCH numbers equal, line counts and prose shares equal.

Every declared fact I checked against the runtime is true, the citations show their values, and every optional fact of 2.1 is declared exactly where the runtime has the behaviour. No shared file was touched, and no other language's page changed.

The one real fault is the one the porter found and recorded correctly as a defect, not hid. Shared code (example.ts refOf) gives the root quick start's list item and its loaded entity the same name. Under C#'s whole-block local scope that is CS0136, so 5 of 21 root quick starts do not compile (crud-bare, crud-basic, crud-noupdate, doc-crud, ex-readonly). OLD compiled. My own scope checker, run over all 1,319 OLD and NEW blocks, finds exactly these 5 and nothing in OLD.

I read the 17 distinct changed blocks of the four variations (31 across all 21) as a compiler would and found nothing else wrong. No compiler checked them: dotnet is missing, so every changed block is still unverified.

The port should be counted only after the shared naming fix lands and csharp re-runs clean. Smaller fixes are listed: a wrong line citation in a hand record, a comment-leaning citation, and a forms reason.

I made 37 attacks. Most failed loudly. These did not fail mechanically:
- B1 and B3: a cited token value whose tokens all stand in the quote.
- H1: a static signature written without its qualifier.
- M1: a cast to a type the runtime lacks.
- L2 and L4: a call to a missing member, or on the wrong receiver, edited into a page. callcheck's MEMBER and RECEIVER findings never fired.
- L1: an example line changed.
Each of these surfaced only as an open class that a porter can close by hand.

required_fixes.change: Print the key through r.key('callopts', ['signal']), and let a fact name what the signal must be (CancellationToken in csharp). Today it is the literal '`callopts.signal`'.
required_fixes.why: On csharp (and on py, rb and lua) `callopts.signal` is not how the key is written (callopts["signal"]). A C# reader is not told that only a CancellationToken is honoured (EntityBase.fragment.cs:267-270). This is awkward, not false.

required_fixes.why: Ran: container 'Dictionary<string, object>' and 'Dictionary<object?, string>' both passed the guard, because every token stands in the quote 'public ProjectNameSDK(Dictionary<string, object?>? options = null)'.

gaps_judged.gap: Root quick start: list item and loaded entity share one name (CS0136)
gaps_judged.why: Real, and csharp alone among the seven has whole-block local scope (java, kotlin, scala, cpp, js and php accept it; read). The existing interface could avoid it only by an unidiomatic `each` printer (List.ForEach with a lambda, legal under C# 8 shadowing; read, not compiled), not by any name change. So recording it as a defect plus an additive gap is the right call.

hypotheses.evidence: 0 breaking changes and 1 additive gap. The provider reads no model; the hook calls nom and csVarName, both also called by TestEntity_csharp. Language-supplied prose (sharewords, ran): 2.1% of 57,562 words (notes 1.6%, fact literals 0.5%). 'Printed by csharp alone' is 4.1%, well under 15%.
741 lines deleted against 201 for provider plus hook (3.7x), or 254 counting the net forms growth (2.9x). Non-blank, non-comment: 541 against 151.

Eight catalogue ids in the ported sections were fixed by shared code with no csharp-specific code: S49 (40 units), S50 (9), S09 (38), S13, S25, U34, U45, G27. csharp's own corrections (TestSDK, Direct and Prepare defaults) are declared signatures, not edits. The CS0136 regression is new, not catalogued, and needs one shared change.

hypotheses.verdict: cannot be run here; by reading, one failure intrinsic to the approach
hypotheses.evidence: No dotnet, so no example ran, OLD or NEW. Read as a compiler: 5 of 21 root quick starts fail CS0136 because one shared name meets C#'s scope rule; OLD compiled. No other changed block is doubtful beyond implicit usings, which are the same as OLD.

interface: I read Syntax_csharp.ts (176 lines) and Naming_csharp.ts (25). Neither reads the model, an entity or an operation by name; the operation literals live in the fact table. There is no case change, concatenation or reserved list in the provider; csVarName's reserved list is accepted by purity because a code generator calls it. The single note is a csharp-only runtime fact (the Stream's own CancellationToken), and its pin, citation and lint all hold. The forms changes are the porter's and are needed: the old param reader named defaulted parameters after their default. I ran the regexes on sample strings, and reverting the fix makes the guard fail. The cpp, kotlin and scala readers do not have this fault (ran on samples); java has no defaults. The diff stat touches only the files section 4 allows. The tools commit has csharp files only, and the commit bodies are subject lines with no trailer.
